title: Simply supported vs. fixed–fixed deflection
statement: A simply supported beam and a fixed–fixed beam have the same span L and flexural rigidity EI and carry the same uniform load w. Without detailed calculation, explain which has the larger midspan deflection and roughly by what factor.

knownAnswer.description: The simply supported beam, about 5 times larger

given: Same span $L$, flexural rigidity $EI$ and uniform load $w$
Beam 1: simply supported; beam 2: fixed at both ends
find: Which beam deflects more at midspan, and roughly by what factor

referencePlan.method: Compare end restraint, then the standard midspan deflection formulas.

steps.title: Compare the end conditions
steps.latex: \text{Fixed ends resist rotation} \;\Rightarrow\; \text{hogging moments at the supports reduce the sagging at midspan}
steps.rationale: Restraint at the ends takes over part of the bending, so the beam bends less in the middle.
steps.hint1: What can a fixed end do that a pin or roller can't?
steps.hint2: Think about the end moments a fixed support develops and what they do to the midspan curvature.
steps.checkQuestion: Where is the bending moment largest in the fixed–fixed beam?

steps.title: Standard midspan deflections
steps.rationale: These are the textbook results for each support condition.
steps.hint1: Both deflections have the same wL^4/EI form. What differs?
steps.hint2: Compare the numerical coefficients in the two standard formulas.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.latex: \text{The simply supported beam deflects about } 5\times \text{ more at midspan.}
steps.rationale: The ratio of the coefficients is 5.
steps.hint1: Divide one deflection by the other.
steps.hint2: Divide the simply supported coefficient by the fixed–fixed one.
